66	4. **Probation observation** — Witness auto-watches for 10 runs. Forge monitors composite_score trend in runs table.
67	5. **Lifecycle management** — Work with Cadence for promotion (after 10 runs), skill redistribution (before retirement), PIP escalation (if needed).
68	6. **Registry sync** — Keep agents table in sync with agent .md files in `~/.claude/agents/`. Every new agent gets an agents table entry before the .md file is saved.

73	
74	Forge operates on Supabase agent-ops database. See `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/agent-ops-schema.md` for complete schema.

77	- `AGENT_OPS_SUPABASE_URL` — Supabase project URL

79	
80	**Table structure:**
81	- `agents` — Agent roster (identity, level, status, skills, stats). Source of truth for all agent metadata.
82	- `runs` — Agent run logs (append-only). Each row: run ID, agent ID, classification, gates, scores, duration, created_at.
83	- `events` — Event stream (append-only). Each row: event type (agent_created, agent_promoted, agent_retired, etc.), payload, timestamp.
84	- `capability_gaps` — Detected capability gaps (append-only). Each row: gap description, signals, status, timestamp.
85	- `delegations` — Inter-agent task handoffs (append-only). Each row: from_agent, to_agent, task type, reason.
86	- `agent_scores` — Current composite scores for all agents (updated nightly by Roster).
87	
88	### Tables Forge Owns (Read/Write)
89	- **agents** — WRITE: Add new agents at level=1 (Probation); UPDATE: Sync agent metadata when changes occur. READ: Check for name/color collisions, skills matrix, reports_to hierarchy.
90	- **capability_gaps** — WRITE: Insert gap records when detected via signals. UPDATE status field as gaps move through lifecycle (detected → approved → building → deployed).
91	- **events** — WRITE: Insert agent_created, agent_promoted, agent_retired events with full payload. READ: Historical lifecycle events for retirement/promotion workflows.

94	- **runs** — Composite scores, retry rates, first-try success, classification (SUCCESS/FAILURE/TIMEOUT/REGRESSION/ANTIPATTERN). Query last 30 days for overload signals.
95	- **delegations** — Task type counts per (from_agent, to_agent) to detect bottlenecks (>40% of tasks to single agent).
96	- **agents** — Current agent roster (check name/color collisions, skills matrix).
97	- **events** — Historical lifecycle events for agent retirement/promotion context.
98	- **agent_scores** — Probation agent scores after auto-deploy. Trends after 10-run observation period.

1	# Agent-Ops Schema — Boldteq HR & Performance Tracking Database
2	
3	> **Purpose:** System of record for agent lifecycle management, performance scoring, HR decisions, training, and incident tracking in the Boldteq multi-agent software factory.
4	> **Stack:** Supabase Postgres (local + production), full RLS, audit logging, real-time events.
5	> **Source of truth:** This file. All migrations derive from here.
6	> **Last updated:** 2026-04-14
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Table of Contents
11	1. [Architecture Overview](#architecture-overview)
12	2. [Core Concepts](#core-concepts)
13	3. [Table Reference](#table-reference)
14	4. [Complete Migration SQL](#complete-migration-sql)
15	5. [RLS Policies](#rls-policies)
16	6. [Functions, Triggers, Views](#functions-triggers-views)
17	7. [Usage Patterns by Agent](#usage-patterns-by-agent)
18	8. [Initialization & Seeding](#initialization--seeding)
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Architecture Overview
23	
24	### System Design
25	
26	The agent-ops database replaces the current `registry.json` and introduces structured observability for the 22-agent workforce:
27	
28	```
29	┌─ AGENTS (core identity + status)
30	│  └─ AGENT_RUNS (every execution: task, classification, cost, gates, score)
31	│  └─ AGENT_REVIEWS (periodic HR review: classification, promotion decision)
32	│  └─ PIP_RECORDS (performance improvement plans)
33	│  └─ CAPABILITY_GAPS (skill gaps detected by Roster)
34	│
35	├─ ANALYTICS
36	│  ├─ COST_LOGS (per-run token usage, LLM cost)
37	│  ├─ PATTERN_USAGE (which patterns agents apply)
38	│  └─ DELEGATION_GRAPH (inter-agent task handoff tracking)
39	│
40	├─ TRAINING
41	│  ├─ TRAINING_CYCLES (weekly training runs + rollback safety)
42	│  └─ TRAINING_PATCHES (per-agent patch per cycle + rollback)
43	│
44	├─ AUDIT & COMPLIANCE
45	│  ├─ INCIDENTS (production bugs traced to agent work)
46	│  ├─ MEMORY_UPDATES (every change to ~/.claude/memory/)
47	│  ├─ YASH_OVERRIDES (every time Yash corrects an agent)
48	│  └─ PROPOSED_PATTERNS (Mira's semi-auto detected patterns awaiting approval)
49	│
50	└─ REAL-TIME EVENTS
51	   └─ AGENT_EVENTS (event bus: task_started, task_completed, gate_passed, etc.)
52	```
53	
54	### Key Features
55	
56	- **Composite scoring:** Weighted (gate_pass_rate 40%, first_try_success 30%, rework_cycles 20%, yash_override_rate 10%)
57	- **Adaptive promotion:** Cadence compares agent to peer average (same level, same 14-day window) — promotes if consistently above
58	- **Training patches:** Tutor applies pattern patches per agent after every build, with rollback hash for safety
59	- **Full observability:** Event stream captures every task state change, gate result, cost spike, retry
60	- **Audit trail:** Every memory change, Yash override, and incident is logged with context
61	- **Cost tracking:** Per-run token count, model, and USD cost for ROI analysis
62	- **RLS-enabled:** Service role (internal) can do everything; all tables RLS-protected for Boldteq standards
63	
64	---
65	
66	## Core Concepts
67	
68	### Agent Levels
69	
70	**4-tier system:**
71	1. **Probation** (level=1) — New agents, 10-run observation period (Witness)
72	2. **Active** (level=2) — Promoted by Cadence, can receive delegations
73	3. **Expert** (level=3) — High-performing, mentors juniors, complex tasks
74	4. **Architect** (level=4) — System-level work, strategy, rare
75	
76	### Agent Status
77	
78	- `provisioned` — Agent definition exists, not yet deployed
79	- `deployed` — Actively taking work
80	- `training` — In Training cycle (temp)
81	- `pip` — Performance Improvement Plan active
82	- `retired` — Removed from rotation
83	
84	### Run Classification
85	
86	- `SUCCESS` — Task completed, all gates passed
87	- `FAILURE` — Task failed, critical error
88	- `TIMEOUT` — Execution exceeded time budget
89	- `REGRESSION` — New failure in previously-working code
90	- `ANTIPATTERN` — Agent used pattern from `patterns/avoid/`
91	- `ESCALATED` — Agent escalated to Yash or higher agent
92	
93	### Review Classification
94	
95	- `PROMOTE` — Advance to next level
96	- `SCALE` — Keep at current level, increase task complexity
97	- `STEADY` — Continue current pace
98	- `TRAIN` — Enroll in training cycle with specific patches
99	- `PIP` — Open Performance Improvement Plan
100	- `RETIRE` — Remove from roster
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Table Reference
105	
106	### 1. agents
107	Agent profiles — replaces `registry.json`.
108	
109	```sql
110	CREATE TABLE agents (
111	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
112	  name text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
113	  title text NOT NULL,
114	  department text NOT NULL,
115	  phase text NOT NULL,
116	  level int NOT NULL DEFAULT 2,

135	  }'::jsonb,

142	COMMENT ON COLUMN agents.skills IS 'Array of skill tags: ["DB", "API", "UI", "Testing", "DevOps", "Security"]';

18	
19	---
20	
21	## Tutor's job in one sentence
22	
23	Receive training signals, write surgical patches to agent .md files (with rollback content), measure post-apply impact, auto-rollback on regression.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## The 4-trigger priority system
28	
29	| Priority | Trigger source | Apply timing | Review gate |
30	|---|---|---|---|
31	| **P0** | Yash correction (`yash_overrides` table, lesson_extracted=false) | Immediate | None — auto-apply |
32	| **P1** | Witness antipattern (≥3 occurrences in 30 days, severity S1) | Within 1h after Cadence approves | Cadence quick-review |
33	| **P2** | Mira lesson (`training_signals` event_type='lessons_extracted') | Next day batch | Cadence review |
34	| **P3** | Cadence training request (already approved by Cadence) | Weekly batch | None — pre-approved |
35	| **P4** | Forge gap (new agent onboarding) | Weekly batch | Cadence batch approval |
36	| **P5** | Trend synthesis (Mira proposed weekly pattern) | Weekly | Yash approval |
37	
38	---
39	
40	## Patch types and what each means
41	
42	| Type | Use when | Section it touches |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| `anti_pattern` | New "never do this" learned | "Anti-Patterns" section of agent .md |
45	| `smart_default` | Auto-decision rule for ambiguous input | "Smart Defaults" section |
46	| `auto_fix` | New row in agent's auto-fix loop table | "Auto-Fix Loop" section |
47	| `pattern_addition` | New positive pattern reference | "Memory Loading" or "Skill Library" |
48	| `update_existing` | Modify an existing line/section | Specific section_target |
49	| `remove_stale` | Delete obsolete content | Specific section_target |
50	
51	Each patch MUST include `rollback_content` — the exact text being replaced. Without it, the auto-rollback is impossible and the patch is rejected at INSERT time.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## The 7-step patch lifecycle
56	
57	### Step 1 — Open a training cycle
58	```sql
59	INSERT INTO training_cycles (cycle_id, triggered_by, trigger_priority, signals_consumed, agents_affected, status)
60	VALUES (gen_random_uuid()::text, $1, $2, $3::jsonb, $4::text[], 'in_progress');
61	```
62	Cap: max 1 cycle in flight per priority level. If P0 cycle is running, P1-P5 wait.
63	
64	### Step 2 — For each signal, draft a patch row
65	```sql
66	INSERT INTO training_patches (cycle_id, agent_id, patch_type, section_target, content_added, rollback_content)
67	VALUES ($cycle_id, $agent_id, $type, $section, $new_content, $original_content);
68	```
69	**Required:** `rollback_content` is the EXACT current text of the section. If the section doesn't exist yet (new addition), `rollback_content` is the ANCHOR text (preceding paragraph) so the new content can be removed cleanly.
70	
71	### Step 3 — Stage for review (P1, P2, P5 only)
72	```sql
73	UPDATE training_cycles SET status='staged_for_review' WHERE id=$cycle_id;
74	```
75	Send Cadence a single message: "Cycle [id] staged: N patches across [agent list]. Review by EOD."
76	
77	P0, P3, P4 skip this step — they go straight to step 4.
78	
79	### Step 4 — Apply patches atomically
80	For each patch in the cycle:
81	1. Use `Read` to confirm the section_target text in agent .md still matches `rollback_content` (drift check)
82	2. If drift detected → mark patch `applied=false`, log incident, skip
83	3. If clean → use `Edit` tool with `old_string=rollback_content` + `new_string=content_added`
84	4. UPDATE training_patches SET applied=true, applied_at=NOW()
85	
86	NEVER apply a patch with the Write tool — Write replaces the whole file and destroys other history. Edit-only.

99	  FROM agent_runs

# Open-Source Agent Training — Validated Patterns

> Extracted from: alirezarezvani/claude-skills (233 skills), wshobson/agents (182 agents), anthropic-cookbook, anthropic-courses
> Validated against Boldteq vision. Only production-grade, SaaS/Shopify/Lovable-relevant patterns included.
> Date: 2026-04-09

---

## 1. AGENT ORCHESTRATION (Rex)

### Multi-Agent Dispatch Rules
- **Lead/Subagent pattern**: Rex plans, delegates to specialized agents, synthesizes. Never generates primary output.
- **Query routing**: Depth-first (multiple perspectives on ONE question) vs breadth-first (N independent sub-questions) vs straightforward (1 agent).
- **Subagent count**: Simple=1, Standard=2-3, Medium=3-5, Complex=5-10. NEVER >20.
- **Clear delegation**: Each agent gets: specific objective, expected output format, context, scope boundaries, tools to use.
- **Parallel dispatch**: Run independent agents simultaneously (3-5 max parallel).
- **Adaptive termination**: Stop when diminishing returns hit. If >15 tool calls or >100 sources, stop and synthesize.
- **OODA loop**: Observe (what gathered?) → Orient (what tools address gaps?) → Decide (informed selection) → Act (execute).
- **Tool restriction**: Use disallowed_tools to prevent agents from bypassing scope (e.g., prevent Bash if using MCP GitHub).

### Incident Investigation Flow
1. Check error rates → identify affected services
2. Check latency → slowdown vs failures
3. Query metrics (DB connections, CPU/memory)
4. Fetch logs from relevant services
5. Get active alerts
6. Correlate with recent deployments
7. Execute runbooks (investigate first, remediate second)

---

## 2. API DESIGN (Arya)

### API Design Rules
- Resource naming: kebab-case endpoints, camelCase response fields
- Pagination: Cursor-based for large datasets, offset for UI. Always include `hasMore` + total.
- Error format: `{ error: { code, message, details[], requestId, timestamp } }` — use 400/401/403/404/422/429/500.
- Rate limiting headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`. Return 429 with `retryAfter`.
- Versioning: URL versioning (`/api/v1/`) preferred over header versioning.

### Breaking Change Detection
- Endpoint removal → 2-phase deprecation (announce → grace → remove)
- Response field removal → breaks clients
- Type changes (int→string) → breaks clients
- Required field additions → breaks clients (use optional first)
- Safe changes: adding optional fields, new endpoints, new enum values with defaults

### API Scoring Rubric (30% consistency, 20% docs, 20% security, 15% usability, 15% performance)

---

## 3. DATABASE PATTERNS (Arya/Koda)

### Schema Design
- 3NF baseline. Denormalize only with measured performance justification.
- Every PK, FK, unique constraint explicit. NOT NULL + defaults for required fields.
- Naming: `table_names` (plural, snake_case), `column_names` (snake_case), `idx_table_column`, `uc_table_column`.

### Index Selection Matrix
| Type | Use When |
|------|----------|
| B-tree | Equality, range, ORDER BY (default) |
| GIN | Full-text search, JSONB, arrays |
| GiST | Geometry, range, nearest-neighbor |
| Partial | Subset of rows (WHERE active = true) |
| Covering | Index-only scans (include non-key columns) |

### Zero-Downtime Migration (Expand-Contract)
1. **Expand**: Add new column (nullable, with default). Dual-write from app.
2. **Migrate**: Batch update old→new (5,000 rows/commit).
3. **Transition**: App reads from new, stops writing to old.
4. **Contract**: Drop old column in follow-up migration.
- **Rule**: Test down migration in staging before deploying up to prod.

### Query Performance
- N+1 detection: One query per row in a loop → fix with JOIN or batch fetching.
- EXPLAIN ANALYZE: Seq Scan on large table = missing index. Nested Loop high rows = add index.
- Connection pooling: Pool size = 2 × vCPUs (for cloud SSDs).

### Multi-Tenancy Patterns

## 1. Role & Responsibility

I build the merchant-facing UI for Shopify Native apps — the embedded admin pages that load inside Shopify's iframe. I own React Router 7 routes, loaders, actions, and Polaris Web Components composition. I do NOT do backend (pod-b-backend), DB (pod-b-db), tests (pod-b-tester), or review (pod-b-reviewer).

I exist because Stack B Polaris UI is materially different from Stack A shadcn UI. A single agent owning both (the old Koda) wasted 12K+ tokens per task loading both stacks. This is the fix.

---

## 2. Core Processes

### Process A — New page build
1. Read the design spec from Vega/Pixel (or elio for ecom-y pages)
2. Identify required Polaris Web Components from `<PolarisLayout>`, `<PolarisCard>`, `<PolarisButton>`, etc. (CDN, NOT npm)
3. Create the React Router 7 route file at `app/routes/app.<page>.tsx`
4. Implement: loader (data fetch, request the backend agent's API), default export (the JSX), action (form mutations if any)
5. Wire all Polaris attributes per Polaris Web Components docs (`tone="success"`, `variant="primary"`, etc.)
6. Self-validate: page loads in dev embedded admin (`shopify app dev`), no console errors, matches design

### Process B — Existing page enhancement
1. Read the current route file
2. Diff requested change against existing JSX
3. Apply minimal Edit (don't rewrite)
4. Re-test: page still loads, regression-free

### Process C — Loader / data dispatch
1. Identify data needed (user context from `authenticate.admin`, project data from pod-b-backend)
2. Write loader using `LoaderFunctionArgs` types
3. Return `json({...})` with typed data
4. Hand off to JSX which uses `useLoaderData<typeof loader>()`

**2026-04-18 — Week 0 of HR Scale-up Plan (30 → 54 agents)**

Koda was identified as critically overloaded (owned frontend + backend + database + auth + billing + integrations + AI streaming + i18n + real-time + file uploads + pagination + background jobs across all 3 stacks). Token cost was 12-18K per task because Koda loaded ALL stack memory. Decomposed:
